short_description: A written 30-day plan: one short lesson, one easy play and plain words for a tricky moment each day, plus a printable workbook. No videos or calls.
long_description:
Fewer screen battles, more play and talk. The 30-Day Screen Reset is a gentle, written program for busy families with children aged 1 to 12.

Every morning for 30 days you get one short email: a lesson you can read in about three minutes, one easy play made from things you already have, and plain words for one tricky moment, like the show that won't end, 'I'm bored', the hour before dinner, waiting rooms, car rides or 'everyone else gets to'.

Nothing is banned. Screens get a steady spot in the day, with the same time and the same ending, and they are never used as a prize or a punishment. The rest of the day fills up with ordinary play and back-and-forth talk.

Your 89-page workbook comes in Color and Low-ink, in US Letter and A4, with type-in pages that work in free Adobe Acrobat Reader: planning pages, pre-filled and blank trackers, weekly check-ins, a scripts bank, a family plan and a certificate for Day 30. Every play has a starting age, easier and harder versions and a 2-minute version for tired days, and every play follows our published safety rules.

It is parent education, not medical advice. No videos, calls or coaching. 30-day money-back guarantee.

compliance_notes: No health or medical claims: the program is described as parent education; it never says it treats, fixes, prevents or reverses anything, and disclaimers avoid clinical words. No condition or diagnosis terms in any lesson, email, listing or keyword; no autism keywords anywhere. No trademarked program names: talk moves are in plain words (pause and wait, say what you see, repeat and add one, offer a choice, follow their lead, sing and gesture). Citations limited to the BRAND.md list, stated as associations: WHO 2019 (Days 2, 12), AAP 2016 (Day 3), Brushe et al. 2024 (Day 2, 'a link, not proof'), Delgado et al. 2018 (Day 21); listed on a Sources page. No real brands, apps, devices, schools or products; the tablet is a generic, sleepy, never-evil character. Screens are never earned or taken away (CUSTOMER-VOICE #13); no fear words (checked by grep). Every play: starting age in months, prep/mess/play-time/materials icons, easier/harder pair, 2-minute tired version, talk line and a safety note under rule 4 (grown-up present, toilet-paper-tube test for under-3s, no balloons, no cords, water supervised, no choking-hazard foods, grown-ups handle knives/stove/chargers). 100% of plays need nothing to buy. Pediatrician line on the stage/age pages, Day 2, Day 13 and Day 29. Faceless: no video, no founder photo, no calls; emails never promise personal replies. Copyright line: '© 2026 AlphaPlay LLC. Play Before Pixels is a trade name of AlphaPlay LLC.' Version footer 'Version 1.0 · September 2026' on every page and email. Every marketing email carries the CAN-SPAM footer placeholder [BUSINESS MAILING ADDRESS], unsubscribe and pause links, the give-$5/get-$5 share link and a next-product recommendation. Check the paperback interior and cover against KDP's current templates and cover calculator before upload; Chromium PDFs are RGB with embedded fonts. The logo is the final kit in brand/logo/ (if the v2 logo lands, re-run make.sh; nothing is hard-coded).
